  
                              **VISION ROVER**

**Introduction**

This project is a simple obstacle-avoiding robot designed to move automatically without continuous human control. The robotic car uses four DC motors to move forward and change its direction when it encounters an obstacle. The system focuses only on detecting the presence of an obstacle and taking a different direction.

**Problem statement**

A normal manually controlled vehicle requires a person to continuously control its movement. If an obstacle suddenly appears in its path, the vehicle may collide with it. To overcome this problem, an automatic robot can be designed to detect an obstacle and change its direction without manual control.

**Objective**

The main objectives of this project are:

* To design a simple automatic moving robot.  
* To detect obstacles in the robot's path.  
* To avoid collision with obstacles.  
* To automatically change the direction of the robot.  
* To understand the basic working of motors, sensors and Arduino.

**Components Required**

* Arduino Uno  
* Ultrasonic/obstacle detection sensor  
* L298N motor driver  
* 4 DC/BO motors  
* Robot wheels  
* Robot chassis  
* Battery  
* Jumper wires

**Working Principle**

The robot moves forward using four DC motors. The sensor continuously checks whether an obstacle is present in front of the robot.When there is no obstacle, both motors rotate in the required direction and the robot moves forward.When an obstacle is detected, the Arduino sends control signals to the motor driver. The motor driver changes the operation of the two motors so that the robot turns to another direction. After turning, the robot continues moving forward.In this project, the system does not calculate or display the exact distance of the obstacle. It mainly works based on obstacle detection and automatic direction change.

**Procedure**

* Fix the four motors to the robot chassis.  
* Attach the wheels to the motors.  
* Connect the motors to the L298N motor driver.  
* Connect the motor driver control pins to the Arduino.  
* Connect the obstacle-detection sensor to the Arduino.  
* Connect the battery supply properly.  
* Upload the Arduino program.  
* Place the robot on a flat surface and switch it ON.  
* The robot moves forward normally.  
* When an obstacle is detected, the robot changes its direction and continues moving.

**Input and Output**

Input:  
        Obstacle detection signal from the sensor.  
Processing:  
        Arduino checks the sensor signal and controls the motor driver.  
Output:  
        Movement of the two motors and automatic change in direction.

**Program**

// Automatic Obstacle Avoiding Rover  
// Arduino UNO \+ HC-SR04 \+ L298N

// Ultrasonic Sensor  
\#define TRIG\_PIN 9  
\#define ECHO\_PIN 10

// L298N Motor Driver  
\#define ENA 5  
\#define IN1 2  
\#define IN2 3

\#define ENB 6  
\#define IN3 4  
\#define IN4 7

// Servo is not used in this basic version  
// Ultrasonic sensor faces forward

int motorSpeed \= 170;  
int obstacleDistance \= 20;   // cm

// \--------------------------------------------------  
// Setup  
// \--------------------------------------------------  
void setup() {

  pinMode(TRIG\_PIN, OUTPUT);  
  pinMode(ECHO\_PIN, INPUT);

  pinMode(ENA, OUTPUT);  
  pinMode(IN1, OUTPUT);  
  pinMode(IN2, OUTPUT);

  pinMode(ENB, OUTPUT);  
  pinMode(IN3, OUTPUT);  
  pinMode(IN4, OUTPUT);

  Serial.begin(9600);

  stopRover();  
  delay(1000);  
}

// \--------------------------------------------------  
// Main Loop  
// \--------------------------------------------------  
void loop() {

  int distance \= getDistance();

  Serial.print("Distance: ");  
  Serial.print(distance);  
  Serial.println(" cm");

  if (distance \> obstacleDistance || distance \== 0\) {

    // No obstacle  
    moveForward();

  } else {

    // Obstacle detected  
    stopRover();  
    delay(300);

    moveBackward();  
    delay(400);

    stopRover();  
    delay(300);

    // Turn right  
    turnRight();  
    delay(600);

    stopRover();  
    delay(200);  
  }  
}

// \--------------------------------------------------  
// Ultrasonic Distance Measurement  
// \--------------------------------------------------  
int getDistance() {

  digitalWrite(TRIG\_PIN, LOW);  
  delayMicroseconds(2);

  digitalWrite(TRIG\_PIN, HIGH);  
  delayMicroseconds(10);

  digitalWrite(TRIG\_PIN, LOW);

  long duration \= pulseIn(ECHO\_PIN, HIGH, 30000);

  if (duration \== 0\) {  
    return 0;  
  }

  int distance \= duration \* 0.0343 / 2;

  return distance;  
}

// \--------------------------------------------------  
// Move Forward  
// \--------------------------------------------------  
void moveForward() {

  analogWrite(ENA, motorSpeed);  
  analogWrite(ENB, motorSpeed);

  digitalWrite(IN1, HIGH);  
  digitalWrite(IN2, LOW);

  digitalWrite(IN3, HIGH);  
  digitalWrite(IN4, LOW);  
}

// \--------------------------------------------------  
// Move Backward  
// \--------------------------------------------------  
void moveBackward() {

  analogWrite(ENA, motorSpeed);  
  analogWrite(ENB, motorSpeed);

  digitalWrite(IN1, LOW);  
  digitalWrite(IN2, HIGH);

  digitalWrite(IN3, LOW);  
  digitalWrite(IN4, HIGH);  
}

// \--------------------------------------------------  
// Turn Right  
// \--------------------------------------------------  
void turnRight() {

  analogWrite(ENA, motorSpeed);  
  analogWrite(ENB, motorSpeed);

  // Left motor forward  
  digitalWrite(IN1, HIGH);  
  digitalWrite(IN2, LOW);

  // Right motor backward  
  digitalWrite(IN3, LOW);  
  digitalWrite(IN4, HIGH);  
}

// \--------------------------------------------------  
// Turn Left  
// \--------------------------------------------------  
void turnLeft() {

  analogWrite(ENA, motorSpeed);  
  analogWrite(ENB, motorSpeed);

  // Left motor backward  
  digitalWrite(IN1, LOW);  
  digitalWrite(IN2, HIGH);

  // Right motor forward  
  digitalWrite(IN3, HIGH);  
  digitalWrite(IN4, LOW);  
}

// \--------------------------------------------------  
// Stop Rover  
// \--------------------------------------------------  
void stopRover() {

  analogWrite(ENA, 0);  
  analogWrite(ENB, 0);

  digitalWrite(IN1, LOW);  
  digitalWrite(IN2, LOW);

  digitalWrite(IN3, LOW);  
  digitalWrite(IN4, LOW);  
}

**Advantages**

* Simple and low-cost design.  
* No continuous manual control is required.  
* Helps avoid direct collision with obstacles.  
* Easy to construct and understand.  
* Suitable for beginners to learn Arduino and motor control.

**Result**

The Obstacle Avoiding Robot Using Arduino was successfully designed to move automatically and avoid obstacles. The robot normally moves forward and, when an obstacle is detected, it changes its direction using the four DC motors.

![][image3]

**Conclusion**

This project helped us understand the basic concepts of Arduino programming, sensor-based detection, motor control and automatic navigation. It also provides a simple foundation for developing more advanced autonomous robotic systems.

**Advanced Obstacle Avoidance Using Servo-Mounted Ultrasonic Sensor**

The automatic rover is upgraded with a servo motor and an ultrasonic sensor to improve its obstacle-avoidance capability. In the basic system, the ultrasonic sensor detects obstacles only in the forward direction. In the upgraded system, the ultrasonic sensor is mounted on a servo motor, allowing it to rotate and scan different directions.

When the rover detects an obstacle in front of it, the rover stops and the servo motor rotates the ultrasonic sensor towards the left and right directions. The ultrasonic sensor measures the distance to obstacles on both sides. The Arduino compares the measured distances and determines which side has more free space.

The rover then automatically turns towards the side with greater available space and continues moving forward. This allows the rover to make a more intelligent decision instead of turning in a fixed direction.
